+---

+title: 'AG-9: the agents tool gets add agent, edit agent and remove agent, with the layer option'
+---
+## What
+Add the three write operations of AG-9 to `AgentsTool`. They use `AgentWriter` (task `^n693yd3`).
+
+- New file `Sources/FoundationModelsAgents/Tool/AgentsToolWriteOperations.swift` with three `@Generable @Operation` structs, in the form of `ListAgents` (`Sources/FoundationModelsAgents/Tool/AgentsToolOperations.swift`):
+  - `AddAgent` (`add agent`): `name` (the id), `content` (the full text of `AGENT.md`), `layer` (optional).
+  - `EditAgent` (`edit agent`): `name`, `content` (the full new text), `document` (optional, a relative path in the agent folder, default `AGENT.md`), `layer` (optional).
+  - `RemoveAgent` (`remove agent`): `name`, `layer` (optional).
+- `layer` is a string, `user` or `project`, and an absent `layer` is `user` (D175). The `@Guide` text is the same as the `layer` option of the `skills` tool (SK-6). An other value gives a corrective that names the two values.
+- `name` uses the existing name keys of the tool (`agentNameKeys`, `agent` as an alias), so the forgiving-input rules of `start agent` also apply.
+- Each operation: call `AgentWriter`, then `try await context.runner.registry.reload()` (`Sources/FoundationModelsAgents/Registry/AgentRegistry.swift:271`). `reload()` returns after the change is in the change log of the `agents` endpoint, so the AG-8 endpoint sends the change event. The answer names the file path that changed and the layer. After `add agent` and `edit agent` of `AGENT.md`, the answer also gives the diagnostics of the catalog for that id. When the agent is not in the new catalog (a skip), the answer says so and gives the reason, so the model can correct the file.
+- A writer error gives `.failure` with the corrective message of `AgentWriterError`. No gate (D78).
+- Register the three operations in `AgentsTool.operations(of:)` (`Sources/FoundationModelsAgents/Tool/AgentsTool.swift:212`) for `.full` only, after `cancel agent`. `.messagingOnly` does not get them.
+- Add the verb aliases `create` → `add`, `update` → `edit` and `delete` → `remove` to `AgentsTool.verbAliases` when they do not conflict with an existing alias.
+- Update `Sources/FoundationModelsAgents/Tool/AgentsToolDescription.swift`: one sentence for the write operations and the `layer` option.
+- `start agent` of a new agent in the same session works, because `startableAgents` reads the live catalog.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `{"op": "add agent", "name": "reviewer", "content": "..."}` writes `<user layer>/reviewer/AGENT.md`, the catalog then holds `reviewer` from the user layer, and `start agent` with `reviewer` starts it.
+- [ ] The same call with `"layer": "project"` writes `<project layer>/reviewer/AGENT.md`.
+- [ ] `edit agent` with `name: "default"` changes the root `AGENT.md` of the user layer, and `AgentRunner` gives the new default instructions.
+- [ ] `remove agent` deletes the folder, and the agent is not in the catalog after the call.
+- [ ] Each write gives one change event on the `agents` endpoint (`AgentsGraph` changes subscription).
+- [ ] A tool with `.messagingOnly` has no write operation.
+- [ ] A bad `layer`, a bad id and a missing agent give a corrective failure, and no file changes.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] New `Tests/FoundationModelsAgentsTests/AgentsToolWriteTests.swift`: call each operation through the tool with a temporary `user < project` stack; check the files, the catalog after the call, the answer text, the diagnostics of an add with a frontmatter warning, and the skip report of an add with no frontmatter.
+- [ ] In `AgentsToolWriteTests.swift`: subscribe to the changes of `AgentsGraph` (as in `Tests/FoundationModelsAgentsTests/AgentsGraphChangesTests.swift`) and check one change event for `add agent`, `edit agent` and `remove agent`.
+- [ ] Update `Tests/FoundationModelsAgentsTests/AgentsToolSchemaTests.swift` (the pinned schema gets `content`, `document` and `layer`), `AgentsToolDescriptionTests.swift` and `AgentsToolMountTests.swift` (the operation list of each grant).
+- [ ] `swift build --build-tests` gives no error and no warning. `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #step1 #AG-9
\ No newline at end of file
